title: Rationalize compact button states, table density tokens, and publish library patch
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Background: Several product teams have requested a consistent "compact" modality for controls and tables when used in dense UI surfaces (sidebars, list items, inlined controls). Figma library currently contains three overlapping compact approaches: (1) component-level compact variants with duplicated layers, (2) token-based density overrides that only affect spacing, and (3) manual component overrides used in a handful of dashboards. This causes confusion for engineers (multiple props to implement), inconsistent spacing when composing controls inside tables, and extra maintenance when renaming tokens.

Scope: This ticket will (A) consolidate the compact design pattern into a token-first approach (density tokens that cascade to components), (B) simplify button state layers and variant naming so collisions are not present in published libraries, (C) introduce a small set of table cell density tokens and apply them across table atoms/molecules, (D) run an authoring pass to fix Auto Layout constraints so compact variants do not collapse or overflow in edge cases, and (E) publish a patch release with a rollback plan and QA checklist.

Goals:
- Single source of truth for "compact" behavior via density tokens (e.g., density-compact-padding, density-compact-gap).
- Remove duplicate state layers in button components and ensure accessible hit-targets remain >= 40px where necessary.
- Reduce component variants by regrouping into semantic families (btn/primary, btn/secondary) each supporting density via token.
- Provide table cell tokens (table-cell-padding-compact, table-cell-font-scale-compact) and ensure header/body consistency.
- No breaking changes for existing consumers: deprecated component-level compact variants will be aliased and documented for two releases.

Deliverables:
- Updated Figma library page: "UI Kit / Density" with token definitions and usage examples.
- Refactored button components with a maximum of 6 explicit variants (size x state) and density controlled by token.
- Refactored table components demonstrating normal and compact density in side-by-side examples.
- Auto Layout fixes applied across button and table master components.
- PR in design repo with release notes and migration guide: how to map old compact component variants to token usage.
- Published library patch and rollback instructions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Designers can toggle density by switching the density token at the frame/component level and see correct spacing across buttons and table cells.
- Engineers receive a single mapping table in the migration guide (old variant -> new token prop) and no more than one downstream follow-up issue per integrator.
- Visual diff checklist: no spacing regressions greater than 2px in primary product flows; screenshots attached to PR.
- Accessibility: compact primary button must maintain a minimum perceived target size and color contrast standards.

UX decisions and trade-offs:
- We chose token-first approach for long-term maintainability despite a slightly longer initial migration for product teams. This reduces combinatorial variant explosion.
- Kept a small set of deprecated compact variants for two releases to avoid immediate breakage; plan to remove after usage drops below 5% as measured by Console component usage dashboards.
- For very small inline icons, we document an escape hatch pattern (icon-only small variant) instead of shrinking hit-targets below recommended minimums.

Links and references:
- Figma file (working): https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/Redwood-UI-Kit---Density
- Migration doc (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XYZ-design-migration
- Design PR (repo): https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/pull/678
- Console dashboard for component usage: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/component-usage

Notes on publishing:
- Patch release name: ui-kit-2026.03.1
- Pre-publish QA: run token swap across 3 critical product pages (dashboard, inbox, admin-table) and capture screenshots.
- Rollback: Re-publish previous library file and push a short deprecation banner in Slack and the migration doc. Keep alias variants available for two releases.
acceptance_criteria: Density token toggles spacing correctly across button and table examples
Button masters reduce duplicate state layers; maintain accessible hit targets
Table cell tokens applied and consistent for header/body rows
Auto Layout constraints fixed: no overflow or collapse in compact sizes
Migration guide published and linked to PR
Library patch released with rollback instructions
